title: Log4Shell-style error storm from malformed input triggering exception flood
symptoms: Error rate jumped from 1% to 55% in 90 seconds. Logs flooded with: ValueError: malformed log format string in user-agent header. Exception traceback repeated 50,000 times/minute. Application CPU at 100% processing exception logging. Log files growing at 500MB/minute.
root_cause: A malformed User-Agent header containing ${jndi:ldap://...} strings was being passed to Python's logging.debug() which attempted string interpolation. This caused a ValueError exception on every request from that scanner IP (200 req/s). Each exception generated a full 40-line traceback written to disk.
fix_applied: 1. Blocked scanner IP range at nginx level: deny 185.220.0.0/16. 2. Changed logging to use lazy formatting: logger.debug('%s', user_agent) not logger.debug(f'{user_agent}'). 3. Added input sanitization to strip non-printable characters from headers. 4. Set log rate limiting: max 1000 identical exceptions/minute per logger. 5. Added WAF rule to block JNDI lookup patterns in headers.
